jobs.description:
Department Information

Vision

We enhance public safety and promote successful community reintegration through education, treatment and active participation in rehabilitative and restorative justice programs.

Mission

To facilitate the successful reintegration of the individuals in our care back to their communities equipped with the tools to be drug-free, healthy, and employable members of society by providing education, treatment, rehabilitative, and restorative justice programs, all in a safe and humane environment.

Commitment

The California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR) and the California Correctional Health Care Services (CCHCS) are committed to transforming the correctional landscape to create safer, more professional, and more fulfilling environments for our employees, the incarcerated population, and those supervised in our communities. Through systemwide improvements grounded in proven and emerging practices, we aim to strengthen rehabilitation, enhance workplace satisfaction, and support successful reentry into the community through our institutions, parole, and community partnerships. Our shared mission is to promote safety, wellness, and human dignity while fostering positive change for all those who live and work within our institutions and communities.

CDCR and CCHCS are committed to building an inclusive respectful workplace. We are determined to attract and hire candidates from all communities and empower employees from a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and personal experiences. We are proud to foster inclusion and drive collaborative efforts at all levels of the Department.

CDCR and CCHCS strive to collaborate with the community to enhance public safety and promote successful community reintegration through education, treatment and active participation in rehabilitative and restorative justice programs. Incumbents establish and maintain cooperative working relationships within the department, other governmental agencies, health care partners, and communities.

CDCR/CCHCS values all team members. We work cooperatively to provide the highest level of health care possible to a diverse correctional population, which includes medical, dental, nursing, mental health, and pharmacy. We encourage creativity and ingenuity while treating others fairly, honestly, and with respect, all of which are critical to the success of the CDCR/CCHCS mission.

This position in Limited-Term for 24 months and not 12 months as stated above, with a possibility of becoming permanent, in which the incumbent would serve a one-year probationary period.

Job Description And Duties

Effective July 1, 2025, in accordance with the applicable Memorandum of Understanding, the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025) was implemented. PLP 2025 requires each full-time employee in Bargaining Unit 17, and related Excluded, Exempt and Statutory Exempt employees, will have their base salary reduced by 3 percent and will receive 5 PLP 2025 leave credits monthly through June 2027. Salaries do not reflect the recent changes. Part-time employees are subject to the same conditions as full-time employees, on a prorated basis equivalent to their time-base. Permanent intermittent employees are subject to the same condition as full-time employees, based on the number of hours worked in the pay period.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Director, Institution Operations, and functional supervision of the Deputy Director, Statewide Nursing Services, the Assistant Deputy Director (ADD), Nursing Operations provides executive nursing leadership, direction, and oversight for nursing operations across all four regions. The ADD is responsible for advancing institutional professional nursing practice, ensuring high-quality patient outcomes and aligning nursing operations with the organizational strategic priorities. The ADD is administratively responsible for ensuring timely, safe, efficient, and cost-effective nursing practices within CDCR adult institutions. The ADD informs the development of statewide nursing policies, clinical programs, staffing models, and nursing informatics. The ADD functionally supervises the Regional Chief Nurse Executives (RCNE) and participates in the selection of healthcare executives and nursing managers.

Extensive travel is required.

Candidate may be eligible for relocation reimbursement if they meet the criteria requirements.

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Operations & Technology Leadership Track
Reports To:
Chief Operating Officer
Location:
Newport Beach, CA (500 Newport Center Drive) — in-office
Status:
Full-time, Exempt
Position Summary

The Deputy Chief Operating Officer is a high-visibility leadership role designed to develop into the firm's next Chief Operating Officer. This position works side-by-side with the current COO to learn, and ultimately assume ownership of the operational, technological, and people-management functions that keep Tarbox running smoothly. The successful candidate will spend the first phase of the role deeply embedded in current systems and processes, gradually assuming direct responsibility for defined workstreams, with the intention of stepping into the COO seat as part of a planned leadership transition.
This is not a purely administrative or support role. We are looking for a strategic, systems-minded operator who can manage people, run projects end-to-end, and eventually own firm-wide operations independently.
Key Responsibilities

Systems & Technology Coordination

Coordinate the broader technology stack — including Salesforce CRM, Orion, RedBlack, eMoney, Broadridge/ProxyEdge, and Schwab Institutional — ensuring systems are properly configured, integrated, and adopted across teams.
Serve as a firm-wide power user and administrator for Addepar, overseeing data accuracy, portfolio reporting configuration, client-facing output, and integration with custodial and performance data feeds.
Act as the primary liaison with technology vendors and consultants on licensing, pricing, upgrades, and troubleshooting.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows through automation and AI tools, in coordination with the firm's AI strategy initiatives.

People Management

Directly manage a subset of operations, accounting, and administrative staff, with responsibility growing over time to include broader team oversight.
Participate in and eventually lead the annual performance review cycle, including use of Culture Index profiles for hiring, coaching, and development planning.
Support recruiting, onboarding, and offboarding processes, including drafting job descriptions, offer materials, and contractor agreements.
Help manage performance issues, including documentation such as performance improvement plans, in partnership with the COO and outside counsel as needed.

Project Management

Own end-to-end execution of cross-functional projects (e.g., team training, technology rollouts, office/team events, vendor transitions) from planning through completion.
Build and maintain project timelines, budgets, and status reporting for firm leadership.
Manage outside vendors and contractors on discrete projects (e.g., branded materials, marketing collateral, facilities).
Contribute to HR administration, benefits coordination, and day-to-day office operations.

Leadership Development Track

Work directly with the current COO on a structured knowledge-transfer plan covering compliance, operations, HR, marketing, and technology oversight.
Take on increasing decision-making authority over a defined transition period, culminating in readiness to assume the Chief Operating Officer role.
Represent the firm in select external settings (e.g., industry organizations, vendor relationships) to build the relationships needed to lead operations independently.
Ultimately support the CEO in implementing the vision and goals of the firm.

Qualifications

Required

5+ years of operations, business management, or systems administration experience, ideally within a registered investment advisor, family office, or wealth management firm.
Direct hands-on experience with Addepar, including data management, reporting, and administration.
Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple business systems/platforms and driving adoption across teams.
Proven people management experience, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.
Strong project management skills, with a track record of independently driving initiatives to completion.
Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and discretion in handling confidential client and firm information.

Preferred

Experience with additional wealth management technology (Salesforce, Orion, RedBlack, eMoney, Broadridge, Schwab Institutional).
Familiarity with RIA regulatory and compliance obligations (Form ADV, Reg S-P, Marketing Rule, recordkeeping requirements).
Bachelor's degree in business, finance, or related field; CFA, CFP, or PMP credentials are a plus but not required.
Prior experience in a designated successor or leadership-development role.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first year, the Deputy COO has taken ownership of Addepar administration and at least one major cross-functional project and is managing a portion of the operations team directly. By the end of the defined transition period, the Deputy COO is fully prepared to step into the Chief Operating Officer role, with established relationships across the firm, vendors, and where applicable regulators.

We invest in the most promising research to turn ideas into life-changing therapies and devices. We work with government, regulatory officials, and insurance companies to address issues that impact the T1D community -- breaking through barriers that limit access to care worldwide. We provide resources and guidance that makes it easier to live and thrive with T1D. This is more than a moment -- we're empowering a movement for the T1D community. Share your support and help educate and empower individuals facing type 1 diabetes.

Our mission is to improve lives today and tomorrow by accelerating life changing breakthroughs to treat, prevent and ultimately, cure T1D and its complications. Always, we are guided by a single purpose: As we drive towards curing type 1 diabetes, we help make everyday life better for the people who face it.

The Development Director (DD) at Breakthrough T1D is integral in the day-to-day execution of integrated fundraising efforts to support our organizational strategy and mission. Their relationships with constituents and donors on behalf of Breakthrough T1D will ensure the expansion of our reach to support maximum chapter and event growth to further our mission.

As one of the top performing territories in the country, the Southern California and Hawaii territory plays a vital role in the organization’s success. Fundraising & Engagement – 60%

Responsible for achieving both personal and event level revenue goals and support the achievement of chapter revenue and engagement goals.
In collaboration with national and chapter partners, create and implement annual strategies that will drive growth of assigned event portfolio through corporate and individual donor engagement and stewardship at the chapter level. Develop and implement stewardship strategies of all event supporters that align to program standards; ensuring they are done timely and consistently throughout the year
Deploy tactics and strategies within event portfolio that drive foundation and pipeline building activities in support of long-term success of organization

Acquire, cultivate, and solicit mid and major level Fund A Cure donors
Design, plan and implement cultivation event(s) that will inspire and engage key event donors and volunteers.
Develop and implement meaningful audience development strategies that inspire giving night-of, including maximizing table spend and activation
Oversees and develops the Inland Empire Market, a critical developing market within the Greater Orange County Chapter, including identification of volunteer leaders, supporters, and donors to establish the support needed to strengthen this market and execute a fundraising event in our next fiscal year.

Volunteer Management – 20%

Recruit, cultivate, and manage volunteer leaders that drive revenue as key partners; includes event leadership and committees
Ensure meaningful engagement of volunteers at all levels and engage in good working relationships with key volunteer partners.
Partner with volunteer leadership to solicit funding and other support from individuals, corporations, foundations and other sources of funding and/or influence.

Awareness – 10%

Support and maintain the vision, mission, and priorities of Breakthrough T1D. Understand and be able to articulate the strategic direction and purpose of the organization.
Demonstrate an educated and enthusiastic understanding of Breakthrough T1D’s mission and research therapeutics. Promote mission engagement opportunities throughout the community in the areas of research, advocacy, and community engagement and clinical trials.
Represent the interests, professionalism, and integrity of Breakthrough T1D in all activities and relationships through a commitment to organizational standards and leadership by personal example.

Provide leadership, performance management and professional staff development to direct reports.
Maintain departmental and organization-wide policies and procedures
Develops expertise in fundraising management platforms, as appropriate.
Participate in monthly strategy meetings with fundraising events program partners to monitor KPI progress, identify risks and opportunities, and take actions as appropriate to ensure success of event(s).
Partner annually with national program partner(s) to establish budget and pipeline strategies specific to event portfolio and role.

Requirements

5-7 years of fundraising experience, with a clear record of achievement in a complex, mission-driven organization with revenue responsibilities more than $750k; experience working directly or leading staff teams particularly in large scale events (walk, gala, etc.). Strong skills in the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and on-going stewardship of donors and supporters.
In the Signature Events/gala space a history of securing and retaining table hosts, guests, event sponsors and donors.
Experience partnering with strong and active volunteer leaders, including working successfully with a large network of passionate volunteers.
Demonstrate a high degree of energy, integrity, courage, empathy, and creativity. High emotional IQ. Superior active listening, analytical, and critical thinking skills. A team player who can achieve individual objectives and support those of the entire chapter team.
Proven ability to develop and successfully maintain an extensive network of strategic relationships (donors, volunteers, community partners, etc.) in the local area. Existing knowledge and network of relationships in the territory preferred.
Ability to be an enthusiastic spokesperson/representative of Breakthrough T1D’s mission. Clear communicator with ability to inspire others to engage and support an organization’s mission.
Highly efficient in time management and able to meet deadlines under pressure.
College degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Orange County Power Authority seeks a seasoned, collaborative communications and external affairs leader

OCPA is a dynamic public agency serving customers with renewable energy options at stable rates.
A Community Choice Aggregator (CCA) alongside 24 others across the state of California, OCPA launched service in 2022 and currently serves over 181,000 customer accounts in Southern California Edison territory. Current member cities include Buena Park, Fullerton, Irvine, and Fountain Valley with the goal of strategic growth across Orange County. For more information, please visit our website at www.ocpower.org. 
About the Position: The Director of Communications and External Affairs will lead
OCPA’s communications, marketing, external affairs, customer care, community engagement, and customer programs functions. This highly visible leadership role works closely with the CEO, executive team, Board of Directors, member agencies, elected officials, community organizations, business partners, and customers to strengthen public trust, promote OCPA’s clean energy programs and services, and guide strategic communications, media relations, public outreach, and customer engagement.
The successful candidate will be a collaborative and strategic leader who is comfortable working in a public agency environment, building relationships across diverse stakeholder groups, and translating complex issues into clear, effective communications.

Hospitality is about people.

Multi-unit restaurant operations and performance
Development and coaching of GMs and restaurant leadership

SOPs and scalable operational systems
Manager training and leadership development

Operational audits and continuous improvement

Cross-functional collaboration with CEO and HQ leadership
Building the infrastructure needed for continued expansion

The ideal candidate brings 7+ years of progressive multi-unit restaurant operations experience

Experience across both QSR / fast casual and full-service restaurants

Excellent P&L and financial acumen
Experience building SOPs, training programs and scalable systems

The ability to balance high standards with a positive, collaborative leadership style

Position Overview:

Jewish National Fund-USA seeks an Executive Director to oversee a multi-million-dollar fundraising campaign across Northern California.
This leadership portfolio includes board and volunteer development and management of the Northern California campaign team. The Executive Director will work with the National Campaign Director to develop and implement fundraising strategies in alignment with the National Annual Campaign Plan.

The Executive Director's main priorities will include expanding Jewish National Fund USA's annual giving through major gifts, general campaign gifts, new donor identification and cultivation, day to day management of operations, and overseeing all aspects of the annual campaign. Building and maintaining strong relationships with existing donors and strategically expanding the fundraising portfolio to support Jewish National Fund USA's growth in Northern California is a paramount priority.

The successful candidate must be an experienced manager and proactive fundraiser who possesses sophisticated leadership and entrepreneurial spirit. The ideal candidate will be collaborative, results-oriented, and passionate for the Jewish National Fund USA mission and Israel. Candidates may come from a variety of backgrounds such as having held a leadership role in the corporate sector, Senior Development Officer or equivalent in a major nonprofit organization, hospital, museum, historical society, major library, or in the academic arena such as a president and/or dean of a college or university. Experience working with or serving on a Board of Directors is essential.

The Executive Director will focus on the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-net worth individuals, foundations and business supporters. The candidate
will also supervise a team of fundraising professionals and, with this team, help enhance Jewish National Fund USA's profile and ensure that the organization is well positioned in a rapidly evolving and competitive environment.

Responsibilities:

Engage in direct and systematic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-net-worth individuals. Direct responsibility for maintaining and building relationships with a portfolio of major gift prospects. Develop strategic annual and long-term fundraising plans and evaluate progress to goals
Steward existing major gift donor relationships; identify and cultivate new major gift donors; renew financial commitments of existing major gift donors
Promote major donor-centric approaches, well-timed solicitation schedules and data-driven program strategy and analysis to increase revenue generation
Foster relationships with financial advisors, attorneys, donors, and other partners who can facilitate the promotion and acquisition of major and planned gifts, bequests, and annuities
Supervise, train, and develop Northern California fundraising staff. Foster a culture of enthusiasm, teamwork, and collaboration among the fundraising team as well as our passionate and committed lay leaders
Build and facilitate philanthropic capacity by maintaining collaborative relations with other organizations throughout Northern California while showcasing Jewish National Fund USA
Work with Northern California leadership to develop Jewish National Fund USA's strategic vision, goal, and strategies and engage committees to assist in the identification, solicitation, and stewardship of current and new donors
Utilize the Jewish National Fund USA Salesforce database to manage donor and prospect relationships
Travel throughout Northern California as needed for donor solicitation and stewardship

Qualifications:

10 years+ of progressive responsibility and experience in fundraising, or proven sales experience in a client-driven business
Extensive experience working with senior-level executives
Strong supervision skills
Significant experience leading and growing successful fundraising/sales functions including building strategies to strengthen and increase funding from a diverse range of sources including individual donors, private corporations, and philanthropic foundations
Excellent decision-making skills and the ability to balance multiple data points, stakeholders, and overall funding landscape in designing and implementing fundraising strategies
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and collaborative environment, as well as an interest in advancing the organization's fundraising function to be even more strategic, innovative, and results-oriented
Strong communication skills including experience in presenting and public speaking
Strong technical skills and experience with Salesforce preferred or similar CRM/data management system
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required

Perks:

Days off for all work-prohibitive Jewish holidays, in addition to the secular US holidays
3pm close-of-business on Fridays
Flexible expense reimbursement for mileage and donor meetings
Top-notch healthcare (including dental and vision)
Parental Leave policy
Employer-paid life insurance
Employer-paid short and long-term disability
403(b) with generous 10.5% employer contribution
Opportunities to travel to Israel

$175,000- $200,000

Pay Type:

Salaried

WHAT WE DO

For 125 years, Jewish National Fund-USA has helped strengthen the land and people of Israel by investing in the communities, infrastructure, and leadership that shape the country’s future. Our work is focused on making Israel’s North and South places where families can build full, vibrant lives with access to medical care, emergency response, water solutions, parks, playgrounds, jobs, and economic opportunity. Working with our donors and partners, we support underpopulated communities, help attract new residents, improve quality of life, and create the conditions for long-term growth. Our work reaches beyond projects on the ground. Through education, travel, and leadership opportunities, we connect Americans of all ages to Israel in meaningful and lasting ways. That vision continues with the World Zionist Village in Be’er Sheva, a global center that will bring people together to live, learn, lead, and strengthen the next generation of Zionist leadership. From urgent relief to long-term transformation, Jewish National Fund-USA is helping build a stronger future for Israel and creating lasting legacies for generations to come. Learn more at jnf.org.

• Planted more than 250 million trees
• Built over 250 reservoirs and dams
• Developed over 250,000 acres of land
• Created more than 2,000 parks
• Provided the infrastructure for over 1,000 communities
• Connected thousands of children and young adults to Israel and their heritage

Jewish National Fund prides itself on honoring the pioneers of the past and celebrating their spirit by continuing the pioneering tradition in the areas of technology, environmental progress, community development, water renewal and building the land of Israel for many years to come.
Jewish National Fund affirms the bonds of the Jewish family with their strength of unity, the understanding that each member can make a difference and the collective power to build prosperity, develop innovative solutions and promote the greater good.

OUR CREDENTIALS & PARTNERSHIPS

A registered 501(c)(3) organization, Jewish National Fund is recognized as a 4-star organization by Charity Navigator, America's leading independent charity evaluator, for its sound fiscal management, accountability, and transparency. JNF has also been rated a top charity by the American Institute of Philanthropy and meets the 20 rigorous standards of the Better Business Bureau (BBB) Wise Giving Alliance, and the transparency standards of Tzedakah, Inc. No other Jewish organization meets all these standards.

OUR CULTURE

We are Vi Zion
-driven relationship-based, fast-paced, and Positively Israel!

OUR CORE VALUES

Beyond. We are proud and passionate, vocal, and visionary about Israel and Zionism. We pride ourselves on our out-of-the-box thinking and the great things it accomplishes for the land and with the people of Israel.

Belong:
Stay long. We are an inclusive and diverse workplace welcoming and respecting all cultures, ages, religions, ethnicities, genders, orientations, and physical abilities. Understanding that a work-life balance is crucial to the success of our organization, we are empathetic, understanding, caring, appreciative, and respectful of one another as we strive to develop and retain our professionals and donors for the long-run.
Be Inscribed:
Be the Impact. To walk in the land of Israel and see the impact of our work instills the greatest sense of fulfillment. We strive for each employee to make their mark, leave their footprint, be heard, and feel relevant as together we help ensure the vibrancy of Israel for the next 100 years. We plant the future, not just trees.

Be Kind:
Act with Chesed. At JNF-USA we do not underestimate the power of kindness. We use recognition and praise to motivate teams, individuals, donors, and stakeholders. We are proud of our please and thank you's. We listen and lend a helping hand when a co-worker is challenged. Whether random or deliberate acts, kindness is a key ingredient to our positive workplace and mindset.

Together. Great collaboration between our employees, donors and affiliates in Israel is a priority: everyone matters no matter their role. We recognize that open and inspirational communication, teamwork, and collegiality is a force multiplier in reaching our goals, mission, and vision. Jewish National Fund-USA exemplifies the power of unity.

Mission of the Daniel Murphy Scholarship Fund 

The Daniel Murphy Scholarship Fund (DMSF) unlocks educational opportunities for talented Chicago-area students facing financial need. We partner with Scholars, families, schools, alumni, donors, and community leaders through high school and beyond by providing scholarships, academic programs and personal support so that each Scholar can reach their full potential. 

Founded by the Murphy brothers in 1989, DMSF now offers around 150 scholarships to 8th graders each year, supporting more than 500 Scholars in high school with a 100% graduation rate. Those Scholars are attending roughly 40 different parochial and independent day schools in the Chicago area, as well as 40 boarding schools from coast to coast. For more information, please visit www.dmsf.org.

Position Overview 

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic partner to DMSF’s CEO. The COO is responsible for leading and strengthening organizational operations, managing and supporting the Development team, driving cross-functional disciplined execution of strategic priorities, and helping advance DMSF’s mission through strong operational leadership, and donor engagement support. 

This role oversees day-to-day organizational effectiveness while helping position DMSF for long-term growth and sustainability. The COO works closely with the CEO on strategic planning, fundraising initiatives, board engagement, donor strategy, and organizational development, ensuring that systems, people, and priorities are aligned to maximize impact.

The ideal candidate is a mission-driven, hands-on, highly relational, and strategic leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, can balance high-level strategy with operational execution, and is excited to help support a high-performing nonprofit organization with a $6M+ budget. 

Primary Responsibilities 

Organizational Leadership & Operations 

Provide leadership and oversight of organizational operations, systems, and internal processes to ensure efficiency, accountability, and alignment across teams. 
Lead the implementation of strategic priorities in partnership with the CEO and leadership team.

Identify operational challenges and proactively recommend solutions that improve organizational effectiveness.
Lead, mentor, and develop the Development team (2-3 direct reports).

Fundraising Operations

Support preparation for donor meetings, sponsorship conversations, foundation meetings, and major fundraising initiatives. 
Conduct donor and prospect research and help develop briefing materials, talking points, meeting agendas, and follow-up strategies for the CEO. 
Monitor fundraising progress toward annual goals and support reporting and analysis efforts. 
In partnership with team members and outside agencies, lead operations for our annual Golf Classic (which raised $3.4M in 2026) and other fundraising events as needed. 

Executive Support & Strategic Partnership 

Serve as a strategic thought partner to the CEO on organizational priorities, opportunities, challenges, and growth initiatives. 
Help prepare materials, presentations, follow-up and strategy documents for board meetings, donor meetings, and external partnerships. 
Assist in managing organizational priorities and ensuring follow-through on key initiatives. 
Represent DMSF externally with donors, partners, volunteers, schools, alumni, and community stakeholders as needed. 
Support special projects and organizational growth initiatives led by the CEO. 
Help translate the CEO’s vision and board priorities into clear action plans, ownership, timelines, and measurable outcomes. 

Financial Oversight

Collaborate with the CEO to develop annual program and organizational budgets and manage revisions as needed. 
Provide oversight of all financial procedures, including bill payment, payroll coordination, expense coding, approval processes, and monthly financial review. 
Review monthly financial reports for accuracy and help identify trends, risks and opportunities.
Collaborate with accountants, board finance leadership, and internal team members to ensure all approval processes, reporting requirements, and financial policies are followed and executed in a timely manner. 
Support and coordinate pre-planning and execution for the annual audit and 990 preparation.
Help ensure DMSF maintains strong financial controls, clear documentation, and sound administrative practices.

Work with DMSF staff, vendors and contractors to ensure accurate and timely data entry across all organizational and internal tracking systems.
Develop systems to enhance efficiency and maintain records to ensure the organization is compliant, timely and proactive across all organizational operations.
Identify opportunities to consolidate systems and better use technology, data, and reporting tools to support fundraising, programs, finance, and leadership decision-making. 

Contract, Privacy, and Compliance Management 

Serve as a liaison and provide contract management support for all office, vendor, consultant, technology and service providers. 
Ensure DMSF Privacy and Security Policies are fully implemented and updated as needed. 
Conduct regular risk assessments to resolve vulnerabilities and train staff as needed. 
Help maintain appropriate records, documentation, insurance information, vendor files, and compliance materials. 

Human Resources Management 

Lead all human resource functions, working with supervisors to manage hiring, onboarding, development, performance management, offboarding, payroll coordination, and employee relations.
Oversee DMSF organizational policies and procedures (including manuals), creating or updating policies and procedures as needed.
Stay abreast of human resources laws, policies, and trends; serve as a resource to CEO and leadership and collaborate with them on potential changes. 
Serve as a resource to staff and leadership on organizational policies, expectations, and internal processes.

Demonstrated success leading multiple operations functions (experience in all areas not required): finance, human resources, compliance, data, contract/vendor management, information technology, facilities

 Demonstrated success supporting executive leadership and preparing high-level internal and external communications/materials

Systems-minded:
You are driven and fulfilled by creating, executing, and maintaining excellent and sustainable operational systems, which serve as the backbone of DMSF’s programming and fundraising and propel organizational growth.

jobs.description:
Summary

The Deputy Director of Engineering (DDOE)
is responsible for planning, prioritizing, communi-cating, and executing the engineering work efforts across Trident Research to ensure engineer-ing products and services are delivered on time and within scope. The DDOE works under the oversight of the Director of Engineering (DOE) to manage engineering tasking across multiple disciplines, including Mechanical, Electrical, Software, and Systems, as well as aerospace and materials engineering where applicable, ensuring on-time and on-budget completion of R&D-focused work that prioritizes high-quality, practical solutions over perfection. The greatest resource at Trident Research is our engineering talent, and the DDOE is the frontline manager of this multidisciplinary team. It is, therefore, critical to mentor and coach each team member to achieve individual and team success. The DDOE fosters a healthy, trusting, and growth-ori-ented environment through direct engagement with engineers, aligning with the DOE’s vision for a cohesive engineering team. We recognize our work is R&D in nature in many cases and per-fection is never the goal. To build a healthy team, development of a trusting and growth-oriented environment through engagement with the engineers is key. 

DDOE works closely with the Director of Engineering (DOE) to proactively search for, review, and ultimately recommend new technologies, tools, equipment, and other engineering resources that are ‘right for Trident’ and are reasonable (e.g., business case is sound). The DDOE collaborates with the DOE and the Head of Technology and Research (HTR) to identify and resolve technically challenging aspects of the work and recommend technology investments. While it is the responsibility of the DOE to submit and coordinate with the Executive Team to ensure needs are budgeted and executed accordingly, the DDOE does serve as the eyes and ears for the engineers on the floor to make sure we’re properly resourced to complete the work. 

The DDOE will participate in the full cycle of engineering development, from identifying, recruiting, and training talent through overseeing and engaging on engineering design reviews, to rep-resenting Trident Research in presenting developed solutions and product results to our customers. The DDOE supports the DOE in all phases of the engineering development cycle, ensuring alignment with the DOE’s vision and corporate objectives. A principal goal of the DDOE is the appropriate execution of the Systems Engineering Process (SEP) for the work to be accomplished for the company. The DDOE implements the SEP under DOE oversight, ensuring the use of agile development methodologies to support rapid prototyping and iterative development of minimum viable products. Sound engineering principles are required of all engineers if the team is to be successful, and the DDOE's greatest influence in this regard is the company SEP. 

The DDOE works in partnership with the Program Management Office (PMO). Our Project Man-agers (PMs) are responsible for supervising projects, staying on budget, and are directly accountable to our customers. The DDOE and PMs work together to ensure that Trident tracks and delivers exceptional engineering products and services that meet or exceed customer expectations and contractual requirements. The DDOE coordinates with PMs to resolve programmatic conflicts, communicate delays, and ensure technical excellence in contracted efforts, un-der DOE oversight. It is expected that the DDOE will expend approximately half of their time directly engaged on helping to lead, refine, and ensure technical excellence across all contracted work. 

 Success in this position will require proactive communication (i.e., delays, issues, JIRA tasking, etc.). The DDOE must be a strategic thinker and problem solver, possess outstanding technical engineering skills (particularly with regards to risk management), demonstrate excellent written and oral communications skills when representing the company, and be self-motivated to engage and lead. The DDOE ensures engineering processes are effective and efficient, contributing to the DOE’s vision of intuitive and adaptable processes.

 The DDOE must also have prior experience and demonstrated expertise in conducting research and leading technical teams, technical staff supervision, coaching and mentoring, conflict resolution and career mentoring in a rapid-paced research and development environment. The DDOE helps define positional responsibilities and metrics for engineers with the DOE. The met-rics should roll up into department KRAs and KPIs that are ultimately approved by the president. 

Requirements

Educational and Experience Requirements:

●      Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering Required, a Master of Science or doctorate degree in engineering or related field preferred
●      5 years minimum engineering experience
●      Proven track record of leading world-class engineers in multiple disciples.
●      Experience setting and meeting budget/time goals for project tasking utilizing JIRA .
●      Command leadership skills demonstrating sound judgement and personal accountability, with a commitment to excellence, commitment to mission, and commitment to the team.
●      Excellence in Microsoft Office, Project, and SharePoint products, and Jira required.
●      Experience providing written and oral presentations to internal and external customers.
●      Experience in integrating AI, machine learning (ML), and data analytics into engineering solutions, ensuring robust, secure, and optimized models for edge deployment. 
●      Experience in exploring new technologies and methodologies for military applications, ensuring systems are modular, scalable, and adaptable to evolving threats. 

Other Requirements:

●      Must obtain and maintain a minimum of a Secret Security Clearance
●      Must obtain and maintain a valid passport
●      Occasionally exposed to disagreeable conditions. May work extended hours or weekends. May travel overnight or on weekends.

Key Responsibilities
Engineering Team Leadership 50% 1.   Provide effective day-to-day programmatic resource allocation to the engineering team such that all engineering team members are performing optimally.
2.   Provide consistent and frequent feedback to employees by conducting 1-on-1 meetings with direct reports at least biweekly (travel permitting). These sessions are meant to provide mentoring and coaching on work products as well as engagement on work satisfaction, growth opportunities and personal connection within the team.
3.   Provide at least one threads comment per direct report per month.
4.   Identify training plan and career growth track for each direct report semi-annually.
5.   Maintain a record of your team’s skill. Update at least semi-annually.
6.   Monitor and update job descriptions semi-annually for your team members as necessary so that the appropriate duties and responsibilities are captured. This should be done in advance of performance reviews.
7.   Consistently issue and monitor work tasking so that each team member has ample direction and work for a two week time period. Adjustments to priorities can be made, but we must ensure that all team members are engaged.
8.   Work is to be peer reviewed by engineering personnel prior to delivery to the PM to ensure efforts are completed and without error. Draw lessons learned and adjust follow-on tasks accordingly. 
9.   Work with HR and management to execute staff hiring, counseling, or terminations as necessary to create a stellar team. Do not avoid difficult conversations which can create disharmony in the team.
10. Invest time in understanding the latest technology advances within your scope to recommend investments where possible to advance the company’s capabilities.
11. Provide recommendations on team processes, procedures, tools, resources, and facilities improvements to DOE for corporate investment when requested by DOF & ET annually (October) and as needed throughout the year.
12. Perform formal performance evaluations for each team member at least twice per year, highlighting specific accomplishments on specific tasking and identifying areas where improvement can be obtained or where new skills will be required for future envisioned work tasking. Include a candid discussion on personal goals and ensure those are captured and reviewed.
13. Report tasking progress at each milestone to the DOE, ensuring lessons learned are drawn and follow-on tasks are adjusted accordingly.
14. Contribute to the integration of AI, machine learning, and data analytics into sensor systems for real-time data processing, predictive maintenance, and autonomous decision-making under DOE guidance.
15. Support the exploration of new technologies and methodologies for military applications, ensuring systems are modular, scalable, and adaptable under DOE oversight.

Department and Cross-Department Communication 20% 1.   Communications with PM’s: verify work is being completed effectively on-time and within scope, reporting of any potential or know delays, negotiation of hours and scope on tasking, etc. 
2.   Coordinate with PMs to resolve programmatic conflicts, such as resource allocation or schedule adjustments, and communicate delays promptly to ensure contract compliance and customer satisfaction under DOE oversight.
3.   Cross Department Communication – DDOE often must communicate with other departments inside of Trident. Communication should be respectful and timely so that all departments have the information they need in order to meet their respective objectives.

Jira Management 30% 1.   Allocate resources in Jira to effectively complete the work on-time

3.   Enter project Epic level tasks with estimates as allocated in the PMO EP
4.   Communication with engineering team members regarding Jira tasking being updated according to the work being completed

Summary

The Deputy Director of Engineering (DDOE)
is responsible for planning, prioritizing, communi-cating, and executing the engineering work efforts across Trident Research to ensure engineer-ing products and services are delivered on time and within scope. The DDOE works under the oversight of the Director of Engineering (DOE) to manage engineering tasking across multiple disciplines, including Mechanical, Electrical, Software, and Systems, as well as aerospace and materials engineering where applicable, ensuring on-time and on-budget completion of R&D-focused work that prioritizes high-quality, practical solutions over perfection. The greatest resource at Trident Research is our engineering talent, and the DDOE is the frontline manager of this multidisciplinary team. It is, therefore, critical to mentor and coach each team member to achieve individual and team success. The DDOE fosters a healthy, trusting, and growth-ori-ented environment through direct engagement with engineers, aligning with the DOE’s vision for a cohesive engineering team. We recognize our work is R&D in nature in many cases and per-fection is never the goal. To build a healthy team, development of a trusting and growth-oriented environment through engagement with the engineers is key. 

DDOE works closely with the Director of Engineering (DOE) to proactively search for, review, and ultimately recommend new technologies, tools, equipment, and other engineering resources that are ‘right for Trident’ and are reasonable (e.g., business case is sound). The DDOE collaborates with the DOE and the Head of Technology and Research (HTR) to identify and resolve technically challenging aspects of the work and recommend technology investments. While it is the responsibility of the DOE to submit and coordinate with the Executive Team to ensure needs are budgeted and executed accordingly, the DDOE does serve as the eyes and ears for the engineers on the floor to make sure we’re properly resourced to complete the work. 

The DDOE will participate in the full cycle of engineering development, from identifying, recruiting, and training talent through overseeing and engaging on engineering design reviews, to rep-resenting Trident Research in presenting developed solutions and product results to our customers. The DDOE supports the DOE in all phases of the engineering development cycle, ensuring alignment with the DOE’s vision and corporate objectives. A principal goal of the DDOE is the appropriate execution of the Systems Engineering Process (SEP) for the work to be accomplished for the company. The DDOE implements the SEP under DOE oversight, ensuring the use of agile development methodologies to support rapid prototyping and iterative development of minimum viable products. Sound engineering principles are required of all engineers if the team is to be successful, and the DDOE's greatest influence in this regard is the company SEP. 

The DDOE works in partnership with the Program Management Office (PMO). Our Project Man-agers (PMs) are responsible for supervising projects, staying on budget, and are directly accountable to our customers. The DDOE and PMs work together to ensure that Trident tracks and delivers exceptional engineering products and services that meet or exceed customer expectations and contractual requirements. The DDOE coordinates with PMs to resolve programmatic conflicts, communicate delays, and ensure technical excellence in contracted efforts, un-der DOE oversight. It is expected that the DDOE will expend approximately half of their time directly engaged on helping to lead, refine, and ensure technical excellence across all contracted work. 

 Success in this position will require proactive communication (i.e., delays, issues, JIRA tasking, etc.). The DDOE must be a strategic thinker and problem solver, possess outstanding technical engineering skills (particularly with regards to risk management), demonstrate excellent written and oral communications skills when representing the company, and be self-motivated to engage and lead. The DDOE ensures engineering processes are effective and efficient, contributing to the DOE’s vision of intuitive and adaptable processes.

 The DDOE must also have prior experience and demonstrated expertise in conducting research and leading technical teams, technical staff supervision, coaching and mentoring, conflict resolution and career mentoring in a rapid-paced research and development environment. The DDOE helps define positional responsibilities and metrics for engineers with the DOE. The met-rics should roll up into department KRAs and KPIs that are ultimately approved by the president.

●      5 years minimum engineering experience
●      Proven track record of leading world-class engineers in multiple disciples.
●      Experience setting and meeting budget/time goals for project tasking utilizing JIRA .
●      Command leadership skills demonstrating sound judgement and personal accountability, with a commitment to excellence, commitment to mission, and commitment to the team.
●      Excellence in Microsoft Office, Project, and SharePoint products, and Jira required.
●      Experience providing written and oral presentations to internal and external customers.
●      Experience in integrating AI, machine learning (ML), and data analytics into engineering solutions, ensuring robust, secure, and optimized models for edge deployment. 
●      Experience in exploring new technologies and methodologies for military applications, ensuring systems are modular, scalable, and adaptable to evolving threats. 

Other Requirements:

●      Must obtain and maintain a valid passport
●      Occasionally exposed to disagreeable conditions. May work extended hours or weekends. May travel overnight or on weekends.

Engineering Team Leadership 50% 1.   Provide effective day-to-day programmatic resource allocation to the engineering team such that all engineering team members are performing optimally.
2.   Provide consistent and frequent feedback to employees by conducting 1-on-1 meetings with direct reports at least biweekly (travel permitting). These sessions are meant to provide mentoring and coaching on work products as well as engagement on work satisfaction, growth opportunities and personal connection within the team.
